claims.text: Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 is a dual-nanoprecipitation high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy is in an as-manufactured additive-manufacturing condition.
High-temperature oxidation causes elemental migration from nanoprecipitates in this alloy.
Elemental redistribution within nanoprecipitates primarily drives the formation of transient protective oxide scales.
Nanoprecipitate compositional redistribution mediates the local formation and evolution of oxide phases.
Migration of elements from nanoprecipitates leads to preferential formation of protective oxide layers.
Redistribution of key alloying elements can encourage or hinder oxide-scale adherence and stability.
Nanoprecipitate elemental redistribution affects oxidation kinetics.
In situ high-resolution TEM can visualize nanoprecipitate and oxide evolution in real time during oxidation.
Concurrent spatially resolved EDS mapping can identify elemental redistribution within nanoprecipitates during oxidation.
Compositional shifts within nanoprecipitates will correlate with nucleation and growth of a fine, possibly transient, protective oxide scale.
Oxidation behavior in the AM alloy will be markedly different from that of cast and wrought counterparts.
Cast and wrought counterparts lack the additive-manufacturing-induced nanoprecipitate distribution.
Nanoprecipitate-mediated oxide evolution could explain enhanced oxidation resistance in the AM variant.
Nanoprecipitate-mediated oxide evolution could explain enhanced mechanical properties in the AM variant.
The observed oxidation response may depend on AM process parameters.
The findings may not extrapolate to other HEA compositions or nanoprecipitate structures.
